sources.title: Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, General State Space Markov Chains and MCMC Algorithms, Probability Surveys 1 (2004; corrigendum 2023)
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted corrected 64-page PDF; §§3.1–3.4, §§4.2–4.6, and Appendix Lemma 34.
sources.reading_verification: The complete corrected PDF was opened and inspected. Read the definitions, Theorems 4, 8, 9 and 12, the full proofs of Lemmas 20 and 21, and Appendix Lemma 34 including its cyclic-class construction. The survey explicitly omits the proof of Jain–Jamison Theorem 19; that gap is closed locally from the independent full textbook proof by Douc et al. No theorem excerpt substitutes for a local proof.

searches.query: Roberts Rosenthal General State Space Markov Chains Lemma 34 aperiodic minorisation times proof
searches.outcome: Located the complete author-hosted PDF and inspected the full Appendix Lemma 34 proof.

contents.name: General-state irreducibility and aperiodicity conventions
contents.support: The source gives general-state accessibility and cyclic-period conventions; local definitions state the countable-generation and invariant-law hypotheses used here.

contents.name: Stationary positive-set hitting lemma
contents.support: The full stationary contradiction proof, including its two claims and the bound growing linearly in the number of visits, was reconstructed locally.

contents.name: Jain–Jamison positive-measure small-set existence theorem
contents.reason: The survey states this theorem but explicitly omits its proof; the complete proof is supplied locally from Douc et al., Theorem 9.2.6 and Appendix 9.A.

contents.name: Almost-everywhere convergence and pair-coupling route
contents.support: The survey gives the stationary pair-chain coupling route; the local proof supplies pair irreducibility, split, and failed-attempt details.

contents.name: Harris recurrence upgrades stationary-a.e. convergence
contents.support: The source distinguishes stationary-a.e. convergence from the all-start Harris case; the local proof verifies the upgrade.

contents.name: Whole-space minorization implies uniform geometric convergence
contents.support: The source uses a common minorization; the local proof proves residual-kernel contraction for every time.

contents.name: Drift and small-set minorization imply geometric ergodicity
contents.support: The local proof reduces to a bounded small set and supplies the explicit weighted bound through the bivariate coupling lemma.

contents.name: Bivariate drift/minorization coupling estimate
contents.support: The complete split-coupling and supermartingale estimate is written locally, with the residual-moment condition explicit.

contents.name: Aperiodic minorization times are eventually consecutive
contents.support: The appendix proves nonempty additive return times, rules out a nontrivial gcd by a cyclic partition, and applies the numerical-semigroup argument.

contents.name: Petite-set drift enlargement and petite-to-small route
contents.support: The local proof derives randomized-time minorization from the killed drift kernel and proves the fixed-time conversion under the shared-minorizer interface.

contents.name: Null-set starting-state counterexample
contents.support: The product survival probability and its positive limiting value are recomputed for the stated integer chain.

contents.name: Central limit theorems and asymptotic variance material
contents.reason: The assigned page ends at transition-law convergence and geometric mixing; CLT and asymptotic-variance claims belong to later BCS-33 material.

contents.name: Drift/minorization calculation for a Metropolis kernel
contents.support: The source works through a drift/small-set certificate for an exponential-target Metropolis chain; the local theorem proves the general-state V-weighted conclusion.

contents.name: Geometric ergodicity need not ensure a practical finite-run result
contents.support: The examples show that asymptotic ergodicity can coexist with practically misleading finite runs; the local two-state family verifies a diverging mixing time exactly.

sources.title: Randal Douc, Eric Moulines, Pierre Priouret, and Philippe Soulier, Markov Chains
sources.locator: Complete author-hosted 775-page textbook; Chapter 9, §9.A (printed pp. 215–220), plus §9.4 Definition 9.4.1.
sources.reading_verification: The complete author-hosted textbook was retrieved and its full text inspected. Read Proposition 9.A.2, Lemma 9.A.4, Lemma 9.A.5, the complete proof of Theorem 9.2.6, and the petite-set definition. The argument was followed line by line and rewritten with local hypotheses and intermediate items.

searches.query: Douc Moulines Priouret Soulier Markov Chains Theorem 9.2.6 proof small set
searches.outcome: Located the full author-hosted textbook and read the complete Appendix 9.A proof.

contents.name: Jointly measurable kernel Lebesgue decomposition
contents.support: The source constructs the density from increasing finite partitions and a nonnegative martingale; the local proof also handles sigma-finite references by equivalent finite weighting.

contents.name: Iterated kernel densities and convolution inequalities
contents.support: Recursive density versions, convolution lower bounds, and almost-everywhere positivity are proved with the singular-residual argument.

contents.name: Uniform overlap of sections from a positive triple set
contents.support: The finite-partition density point, Fubini section estimates, and three-quarter intersection argument are proved locally.

contents.name: Accessible positive-measure small-set existence
contents.support: The full construction is included locally, including density thresholds, positive section sets, the common-time minorization, and the minorizer charging the small set.

contents.name: General petite-to-small conversion for arbitrary petite sets
contents.reason: The general theorem is not imported without its full interface; the local conversion proves the exact same-minorizer, accessible-subset case needed by the drift reduction.

contents.name: Petite-set definition and randomized-time minorization
contents.support: The local definition states a probability mixing law on positive integer times and an explicit positive common-mass multiplier.
